questions.prompt: What is an AMI in Amazon EC2?

options.text: The template (operating system plus software) an instance boots from
The hardware profile (vCPU and memory) of the instance
The firewall attached to the instance

questions.explanation: An Amazon Machine Image is the launch template — an OS plus any preinstalled software. The hardware profile is the instance type, and the firewall is the security group.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between stopping and terminating an instance?

options.text: Stopping keeps the EBS data and pauses compute charges; terminating permanently deletes the instance
Terminating pauses charges but keeps the instance

questions.explanation: Stop shuts down the OS but keeps the EBS volume and lets you start again; terminate permanently deletes the instance (and, by default, its root volume).

questions.prompt: Order the main choices you make when launching an EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: The launch flows image → hardware → login → firewall → storage (with optional user data before launching).

questions.prompt: Who keeps the private key of an EC2 key pair?

options.text: AWS keeps it on the instance
You do — AWS keeps the public key; you download and store the private key

questions.explanation: AWS stores the public key; you download and safeguard the private key (.pem). Lose it and you can't SSH in the normal way.

questions.prompt: The stateful, allow-only virtual firewall attached to an EC2 instance is called a security ____.
questions.explanation: A security group is a stateful, allow-only virtual firewall controlling inbound and outbound traffic for the instance.

questions.prompt: On EC2 (IaaS), who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?

options.text: You do — the guest OS is the customer's responsibility

questions.explanation: EC2 is IaaS, so under the shared responsibility model the customer patches the guest OS and applications; AWS secures the physical host underneath.
